q: Distance travelled by the body is the length of the path along which the body moves.
e: True. Distance travelled by the body is the length of the path along which the body moves. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start.

q: Displacement is a scalar directed from the starting point to the end point.
e: False. Displacement is a vector, directed from start to end. A scalar does not carry that direction. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: Displacement is the distance travelled along a particular direction.
e: True. Displacement is the distance travelled along a particular direction. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start.

q: Distance has a specific direction.
e: False. Distance is a scalar. It has size only, no direction. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.

q: Distance has only magnitude, and therefore, it is a scalar.
e: True. Distance has only magnitude, and therefore, it is a scalar. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.

q: Displacement has both magnitude and direction, and therefore, it is a vector.
e: True. Displacement has both magnitude and direction, and therefore, it is a vector. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The average speed $v_{av}$ is the ratio of total distance $s$ to time taken $t$.
e: True. The average speed $v_{av}$ is the ratio of total distance $s$ to time taken $t$. The average speed is how fast the path length changes, with no direction.

q: The average speed $v_{av}$ is the ratio of total displacement to time taken $t$.
e: False. The average speed $v_{av}$ is the ratio of total distance $s$ to time taken $t$. This claim used displacement in place of distance $s$.

q: The average velocity $v_{av}$ is the ratio of total displacement $s$ to time taken $t$.
e: True. The average velocity $v_{av}$ is the ratio of total displacement $s$ to time taken $t$. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero.
e: True. If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the average velocity is zero.
e: True. If the starting point and the end point are the same, the average velocity is zero. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The speed and velocity which represent a motion for a certain period of time interval are called average speed and average velocity.
e: True. The speed and velocity which represent a motion for a certain period of time interval are called average speed and average velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The speed or velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as instantaneous speed and instantaneous velocity.
e: True. The speed or velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as instantaneous speed and instantaneous velocity. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: The speedometer of a car indicates the average speed of the car.
e: False. A car speedometer shows instantaneous speed, the reading at that moment, not the average for a trip. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: Instantaneous speed is defined as the time rate of change of distance.
e: True. Instantaneous speed is defined as the time rate of change of distance. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of distance.
e: False. Instantaneous speed is defined as the time rate of change of distance. This claim used velocity in place of speed.

q: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant.
e: True. When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Motion with constant velocity is known as uniform motion.
e: True. Motion with constant velocity is known as uniform motion. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: For a motion with constant velocity, equal displacements take place in unequal intervals of time.
e: False. Constant velocity means equal displacements in equal times. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: If either magnitude or direction or both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an acceleration.
e: True. If either magnitude or direction or both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an acceleration. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Motion with changing velocity is called non-uniform motion or accelerated motion.
e: True. Motion with changing velocity is called non-uniform motion or accelerated motion. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The average acceleration $a_{av}$ is defined by the equation $a_{av} = \frac{v - v_0}{t}$.
e: True. The average acceleration $a_{av}$ is defined by the equation $a_{av} = \frac{v - v_0}{t}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Average acceleration is the ratio of the change in velocity to the distance taken.
e: False. Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Instantaneous acceleration $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{dv}{dt}$.
e: True. Instantaneous acceleration $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{dv}{dt}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity.
e: True. Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is decreasing.
e: False. If speed is falling, that acceleration is negative in the usual 1-D sign choice. Positive acceleration means velocity is increasing that way. Velocity is directed.

q: Negative acceleration is usually called deceleration or retardation.
e: True. Negative acceleration is usually called deceleration or retardation. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.
